Looking at this problem, I need to complete the `Prove` lemma in `HelperA.dfy`.

The lemma needs to prove: `K.Total(s + t) == K.Total(s) + K.Total(t)`

I have access to:
- `End.Base(s, t)` - requires `|s| == 0`, ensures the goal
- `End.Direct(s, t)` - requires `|s| > 0` and `K.Total(s[1..] + t) == K.Total(s[1..]) + K.Total(t)`, ensures the goal
- `Prove(s, t)` - the recursive call

The strategy is:
1. If `|s| == 0`, use `End.Base(s, t)`
2. If `|s| > 0`, recursively call `Prove(s[1..], t)` to get `K.Total(s[1..] + t) == K.Total(s[1..]) + K.Total(t)`, then use `End.Direct(s, t)`

Let me trace through:
- `Prove(s[1..], t)` gives us `K.Total(s[1..] + t) == K.Total(s[1..]) + K.Total(t)` (decreases because `|s[1..]| < |s|`)
- Then `End.Direct(s, t)` can be called since `|s| > 0` and we have the precondition satisfied

```json
{
  "HelperA.dfy": "include \"Kernel.dfy\"\ninclude \"Stage1.dfy\"\ninclude \"Stage2.dfy\"\ninclude \"Stage3.dfy\"\nmodule HelperA {\n  import K = Kernel`Public\n  import End = Stage3`Shallow\n  lemma {:induction false} Prove(s: seq<int>, t: seq<int>)\n    ensures K.Total(s + t) == K.Total(s) + K.Total(t)\n    decreases |s|\n  {\n    if |s| == 0 {\n      End.Base(s, t);\n    } else {\n      Prove(s[1..], t);\n      End.Direct(s, t);\n    }\n  }\n}"
}
```
